bibl.title: A Unified Framework of Five Principles for AI in Society

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: SIX PUBLISHED SETS OF AI ETHICS PRINCIPLES, forty-seven principles in all, read against each other to find out whether they converge - the object is a vocabulary, not a phenomenon
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: how to solve `principle proliferation`: whether the competing declarations say the same thing under different names, or genuinely disagree
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: five principles - beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy and justice imported from bioethics, plus EXPLICABILITY, argued to be new and necessary - claimed to capture all 47
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: method
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a field generating ethical declarations faster than it can reconcile them, with `similar terms often used to mean different things` and a risk the authors name as a `market for principles`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a comparative reading of six sets chosen by three stated criteria - recent, relevant to AI and society as a whole, and published by authoritative multi-stakeholder bodies with at least national scope - mapped onto the four bioethics principles
span.term: a comparative reading of six sets chosen by three stated criteria - recent, relevant to AI and society as a whole, and published by authoritative multi-stakeholder bodies with at least national scope - mapped onto the four bioethics principles
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the convergence is explained by a structural resemblance between the fields, and the explanation is offered rather than tested: `OF ALL AREAS OF APPLIED ETHICS, BIOETHICS IS THE ONE THAT MOST CLOSELY RESEMBLES DIGITAL ETHICS in dealing ecologically with new forms of agents, patients, and environments`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the fifth principle is argued for FUNCTIONALLY - explicability is needed because the other four cannot be checked without it: you cannot tell whether AI is beneficent without understanding what it does, nor hold anyone to account without knowing why an outcome arose
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE SAMPLE IS SIX DOCUMENTS AND THE PAPER SAYS WHERE THEY COME FROM: each `emerged either from initiatives with GLOBAL SCOPE, or from within WESTERN LIBERAL DEMOCRACIES`, and the framework `WOULD UNDOUBTEDLY BENEFIT FROM THE PERSPECTIVES OF REGIONS AND CULTURES PRESENTLY UN- OR UNDER-REPRESENTED`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the coverage claim and the distribution claim are DIFFERENT CLAIMS AND ONLY THE FIRST IS ABSOLUTE: the five principles `CAPTURE EVERY ONE OF THE 47`, but each principle appears in `ALMOST EVERY statement` - and the paper's own Table 1 shows IEEE missing autonomy and justice, and the Partnership missing autonomy
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE ADOPTION EVIDENCE INCLUDES BODIES THE AUTHORS SIT ON. AI4People and the EC High-Level Expert Group are counted as uptake, and the disclosure states that FLORIDI CHAIRED AI4PEOPLE, COWLS WAS ITS RAPPORTEUR, AND FLORIDI IS A MEMBER OF THE HLEG. Declared in full, and it is still the authors' framework being adopted by the authors' committees
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the funding sits on the subject: the work was supported by an EPSRC hub AND BY FACEBOOK AND GOOGLE - two of the companies whose AI the framework is written to govern. Declared
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the paper leaves its central ambiguity open and says so twice: `IT IS NOT ENTIRELY CLEAR WHETHER IT IS THE PEOPLE DEVELOPING AI, OR THE TECHNOLOGY ITSELF, which should be encouraged not to do harm - in other words, whether it is FRANKENSTEIN OR HIS MONSTER against whose maleficence we should be guarding`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and `justice` is left carrying more than one meaning inside the framework that is supposed to fix it: `elsewhere justice has STILL OTHER MEANINGS (especially in the sense of FAIRNESS)`. The unification does not reach inside the principles
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the six documents were selected by three declared criteria - recent, relevant to AI and society as a whole rather than to one sector, and published by authoritative multi-stakeholder bodies of at least national scope
span.note: eliminates: ad-hoc selection as the explanation of the convergence; the criteria are stated before the result and exclude domain-specific documents · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether the convergence is an artefact of where the documents come from
span.note: eliminates: nothing, and the authors say so: all six came from global-scope initiatives or `from within WESTERN LIBERAL DEMOCRACIES`, and the framework would benefit from perspectives `presently un- or under-represented in our sample` · outcome: failed
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether the framework's later adoption is independent evidence for it
span.note: eliminates: nothing - AI4People and the EC High-Level Expert Group are counted as uptake, and the disclosure states the authors chaired, rapporteured and sat on them. THE DISCLOSURE IS COMPLETE AND THE CIRCULARITY IS STILL THERE · outcome: failed
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether `beneficence` and `non-maleficence` are one principle wearing two names
span.note: eliminates: the collapse, explicitly: they `may seem logically equivalent, THEY ARE NOT, and represent distinct principles`, and the six documents treat them separately · outcome: held

span.label: `principle proliferation` - THE CONDITION THIS PAPER NAMES AND TREATS. Either the sets are similar, `leading to UNNECESSARY REPETITION AND REDUNDANCY`, or they differ, and `CONFUSION AND AMBIGUITY will result instead`. The worst case is named too: a `MARKET FOR PRINCIPLES` in which stakeholders `SHOP` for the most appealing
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE DIAGNOSIS, WHICH IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN THESIS IN ONE CLAUSE: `the underlying meaning of each of the principles IS CONTESTED, WITH SIMILAR TERMS OFTEN USED TO MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS`. A shared word list is not a shared vocabulary
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: explicability - FIVE NAMES FOR ONE PRINCIPLE, LISTED WITH THEIR SOURCES: `TRANSPARENCY` in Asilomar and EGE, `transparency` AND `ACCOUNTABILITY` in IEEE, `INTELLIGIBILITY` in AIUK, `UNDERSTANDABLE AND INTERPRETABLE` in the Partnership. The new term is coined to cover a thing four documents already had
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: explicability, as defined - TWO SENSES DELIBERATELY BOUND TOGETHER: the EPISTEMOLOGICAL sense of intelligibility (`how does it work?`) and the ETHICAL sense of accountability (`who is responsible for the way it works?`). One term carrying two questions on purpose
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AI - `A RESEARCH AREA IN SEARCH OF A DEFINITION` in the paper's own heading. It keeps the 1955 Dartmouth formulation, reads it as A COUNTERFACTUAL (`WERE a human to behave in that way, that behaviour WOULD be called intelligent`), and then substitutes its own working phrase - `a reservoir of smart agency on tap` - justified by fitness for the corpus it is about to analyse
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: beneficence and non-maleficence - `THOUGH DO ONLY GOOD AND DO NO HARM MAY SEEM LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT, THEY ARE NOT, AND REPRESENT DISTINCT PRINCIPLES`. A near-synonymy refused explicitly, which is exactly the move most papers leave implicit
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: meta-autonomy - a coined term for `a DECIDE-TO-DELEGATE model`: humans keep the power to decide WHICH decisions to take, and any delegation must remain `OVERRIDABLE IN PRINCIPLE (i.e., deciding to decide again)`
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: extends → Beauchamp & Childress's four principles of bioethics, carried into AI ethics with a fifth added and the imperfection of the translation stated
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: supports → the 1955 Dartmouth proposal's counterfactual formulation of the AI problem, kept as the working definition sixty-four years later
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
